title: automation: tenant RBAC bootstrap for Private installer + Helm/Terraform modules
author: Maya Thompson
description:
Context: Private installer (VPC/on-prem) onboarding requires a deterministic, auditable bootstrap for tenant-level RBAC. Current manual steps are error-prone during automated installs and upgrades (helm + terraform). This PR introduces an automated tenant RBAC bootstrap job and wiring for the private-installer Helm chart and the terraform modules so that fresh installs and upgrades create the minimal set of roles, rolebindings, and automation service accounts required for tenant isolation and operator workflows.

Motivation: Reduce manual operator steps during customer Private deployments and enable reproducible automation for CI/CD pipelines, air-gapped installs, and periodic reconciliation. Prevents a common root cause we saw in INT-589 where missing bootstrapped bindings caused tenant provisioning failures during upgrades.

Summary of changes: Adds a new kustomize overlay and helm hook that runs a one-shot Job to ensure tenant bootstrap resources exist. Adds Terraform module updates to expose a "bootstrap_rbac" flag and an optional service account key rotation schedule. Introduces an RBAC manifest template (parametrized) for tenant-scoped roles and a validation Job that verifies idempotency. Updates installer docs and integration tests.

Migration notes: Default behavior remains off for existing installs. For new installs via the private-installer chart the bootstrap step is enabled by default. Operators upgrading should run `helm upgrade --install private-installer ./chart --set bootstrapRBAC=true` or set `bootstrap_rbac = true` in terraform to opt into automation. Rollback: the bootstrap job is idempotent and will not remove bindings on rollback; it only ensures existence.

Testing and verification: Unit tests for template rendering included. End-to-end integration tests added to perf-canary that exercise a fresh install + upgrade flow in a constrained namespace. CI: all checks passed; a flaky helm lint check was retried once and subsequently passed.

Security considerations: The bootstrap job creates least-privilege roles scoped to tenant namespaces only. Service accounts are created with expiration annotations when run via terraform automation; recommended KMS/HSM policies documented.

Release notes: Added automated tenant RBAC bootstrap for private-installer (Helm + Terraform) to simplify onboarding and upgrades.

Add integration tests and update docs

release_notes: Automation: tenant RBAC bootstrap for Private installer (Helm + Terraform). Default enabled for new installs; opt-in on upgrades. Non-destructive, idempotent bootstrap job.
notes_for_ops: Operators upgrading should enable bootstrapRBAC via helm or terraform. If both helm and terraform are used to manage cluster resources, follow the docs note to avoid duplicate bindings. Bootstrap job creates least-privilege tenant roles and will not revoke existing bindings on rollback.
